raw_extract:
# Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa

You can submit an expression of interest (EOI) if you have a job or job offer from an accredited employer, and meet the requirements for one of the Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) pathways.

Length of stay: Live, work and study indefinitely
Cost: From NZD $6450
Age range: From 55 years or younger

To apply you must:

-   be aged 55 or younger when you apply
-   be working for, or have a job offer from, an and the job is
-   meet the requirements for an SMC pathway, and
-   speak and understand English.

You must submit an expression of interest (EOI) and if accepted, we invite you to apply.

You must be eligible for 1 of the 3 SMC pathways. The Points-based pathway, Skilled Work Experience pathway or Trades and Technicians pathway.

## SMC pathways

### Points-based pathway

You must have 6 points to be eligible for the Points-based pathway. You can claim up to 6 points from either your:

-   qualification
-   income (pay), or
-   occupational registration (for example, if you are a chartered accountant or registered plumber).

If you cannot claim all 6 points from one of these categories, you may be able to claim an additional 1 to 3 points from skilled work experience in New Zealand.

### Skilled Work Experience pathway

To be eligible, you must have at least 5 years of directly relevant work experience, including at least 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand.

### Trades and Technician pathway

To be eligible, you must have a relevant qualification, and at least 4 years of post-qualification work experience, including at least 18 months of skilled work experience in New Zealand.

### Table 2: Skilled resident points you can claim for international qualifications

Qualification | Points you can claim | Bachelor's degree required
Level 10 Doctoral Degree | 6 | No
Level 9 Master's Degree | 5 | Yes
Level 8 Honour's Degree, Postgraduate Diploma or Post-graduate Certificate | 4 | Yes
Level 7 Bachelor's Degree | 4 | Not applicable

### Table 1: Skilled resident points you can claim for New Zealand qualifications

New Zealand qualification | Points you can claim | Bachelor's degree required
Level 10 Doctoral Degree | 6 | No
Level 9 Master's Degree (30 weeks of full-time study) | 6 | Yes
Level 9 Master's Degree (not full-time study) | 5 | No
Level 8 Honour's Degree, Postgraduate Diploma or Post-graduate Certificate | 5 | Yes
Level 7 Bachelor's Degree | 5 | Not applicable

## Check your points

Check if you have enough points to be invited to apply. You need 6 points in total. You still need to meet all requirements and provide evidence in your visa application.

### Table 5: Additional skilled resident points you can claim for skilled work experience in New Zealand

Skilled work experience in New Zealand required | Points you can claim
2 years | 3
1.5 years | 2
1 year | 1

## How long you can stay

A Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa lets you stay in New Zealand indefinitely.

After you have had this visa for 2 years in a row, you can apply for a Permanent Resident Visa that lets you travel in and out of New Zealand indefinitely.

## Requirements for all pathways

All SMC pathways require you to:

-   be aged 55 or younger
-   have an offer of, or be working in, a skilled job with an accredited employer
-   be in good health
-   be of good character
-   have a genuine relationship with your partner and dependent children, if including them, and
-   speak and understand English.

### Current job or job offer

To be considered a skilled job, it must:

-   be with an
-   be and (for at least 30 hours a week)
-   permanent or fixed-term for at least 12 months, or a contract or continuous contracts for at least 6 months, and
-   meet any pay requirements for your SMC pathway.

### Getting citizenship

For most people, after 5 years of living in New Zealand as a resident, you may be able to get New Zealand citizenship. You do not need a Permanent Resident Visa first.

### Section 49 conditions

You must not be unemployed for more than 3 months. If you lose your job, you must get another skilled job that is for at least 3 months to meet your section 49 conditions. If you do not, we may cancel your visa and you must leave the country.
research_notes: STRUCTURAL WARNING FIRST, because it defeats the metric template: New Zealand's residence system for international graduates is NOT a 'minimum years on the qualifying route' system like the UK, Canada or Australia. It is a POINTS system with a job-offer trigger, so no single 'X years' figure is the answer and a corpus row asking for 'years to PR' for NZ should be modelled differently. Route recorded: 'Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Resident Visa', reached through an Expression of Interest, with three alternative pathways - Points-based, Skilled Work Experience, and Trades and Technician. For a BACHELOR'S GRADUATE THE POINTS-BASED PATHWAY IS THE ONLY REACHABLE ONE, and the qualification table is the crucial finding: an international Level 7 Bachelor's Degree is worth only 4 POINTS, against a 6-point threshold, so a bachelor's holder CANNOT qualify on qualification alone and must make up the shortfall - and the page is explicit that the only top-up available is New Zealand skilled work experience, worth 3 points for 2 years, 2 points for 1.5 years and 1 point for 1 year: 'If you do not have 6 points from your qualifications, you can use your skilled work experience in New Zealand to claim more points. You cannot use your occupational registration or income to claim more points.' A DOMESTIC/INTERNATIONAL ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS: the same bachelor's degree is worth 5 points if gained in New Zealand (Table 1) versus 4 points if gained overseas (Table 2), and a New Zealand master's degree completed with at least 30 weeks of full-time study is worth 6 points (an automatic pass) versus 5 points for an international master's. So studying in New Zealand carries a points advantage over studying abroad. Other verified figures: application cost from NZD $6,450; there is no fee to submit an EOI; an ITA must be actioned within 4 months or a new EOI is required; all pathways require the applicant to be aged 55 or younger at application and to hold a skilled job or offer with an accredited employer (at least 30 hours a week, permanent/fixed-term of at least 12 months or contracts of at least 6 months). TIMELINE, which is the closest thing to a 'years to PR' answer: the SMC Resident Visa is granted for an indefinite stay immediately, and 'After you have had this visa for 2 years in a row, you can apply for a Permanent Resident Visa'. Citizenship is separate and later: 'after 5 years of living in New Zealand as a resident, you may be able to get New Zealand citizenship. You do not need a Permanent Resident Visa first.' SUSTAINABILITY RISK THAT IS EASY TO MISS: a section 49 condition may apply, and 'You must not be unemployed for more than 3 months. If you lose your job, you must get another skilled job that is for at least 3 months ... If you do not, we may cancel your visa and you must leave the country.' Not every SMC visa carries one, but where it applies, residence is job-conditional. NOT VERIFIED AND NOT CLAIMED: whether a section 49 condition attaches in a given case (the page says only that they 'are extra conditions we may give to some visas'); the ANZSCO occupation lists; the historic SMC wage thresholds (only the current NZD $105.00 an hour figure and a worked example of NZD $59.32 an hour were printed, and the thresholds are time-varying by design); the Amber and Red List contents; and the Green List occupations. The PhD pathway figure of 6 points is recorded but I have deliberately NOT inferred any PhD-specific scholarship or funding position from it.

claims.statement: New Zealand's skilled residence route for international graduates is the 'Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Resident Visa', a points-based system requiring a job or job offer with an accredited employer, not a simple minimum-years-on-route test.

An international Level 7 Bachelor's Degree is worth 4 skilled resident points against a 6-point requirement, so a bachelor's graduate cannot qualify on qualification alone and must add 1 to 3 points from New Zealand skilled work experience - the only top-up available if relying on qualifications.

The same bachelor's degree is worth 5 points when gained in New Zealand versus 4 points when gained overseas, and a New Zealand master's degree completed with at least 30 weeks of full-time study is worth 6 points versus 5 points for an international master's degree.

New Zealand skilled work experience can supply 1 point for 1 year, 2 points for 1.5 years and up to 3 points for 2 years, and must be in a full-time job of at least 30 hours a week matching the ANZSCO job title and description.
claims.unit: years NZ skilled work experience for the maximum 3 points

claims.statement: A Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa allows an indefinite stay in New Zealand, and after holding it for 2 years in a row the holder can apply for a Permanent Resident Visa; New Zealand citizenship is available after 5 years of living in New Zealand as a resident and does not require a Permanent Resident Visa first.
claims.unit: years on the SMC Resident Visa before Permanent Resident Visa eligibility

claims.statement: All SMC pathways require the applicant to be aged 55 or younger at application, and a Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa costs from NZD $6,450; there is no fee to submit an Expression of Interest, and an Invitation to Apply must be actioned within 4 months.
Where section 49 conditions apply, the visa holder must not be unemployed for more than 3 months and must find another skilled job lasting at least 3 months, failing which the visa may be cancelled.
